# Home & Living — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Home Textiles & Decoration: typically around 1,200, most listings 50–3,000 (44 listings)
- Household Items: typically around 4,000, most listings from ~400 up (23 listings; upper percentile is skewed by one extreme outlier — judge expensive items on merit)
- Living Room Furniture: typically around 25,000, most listings 2,000–90,000 (13 listings)
- Kitchen & Dining Furniture: typically around 3,000, most listings 500–8,000 (12 listings)
- Bedroom Furniture: typically around 7,000, most listings 1,300–23,000 (10 listings)
- Office & Shop Furniture: typically around 1,400, ranging up to ~40,000 (9 listings — thin data)
- Children's Furniture: typically around 2,300, most listings 900–5,300 (4 listings — thin data)

Big-ticket furniture (sofa sets, beds, wardrobes — normally 15,000–90,000) priced far below the low end is a scam or placeholder-price signal → hold. But very low prices (NPR 50–500) are normal for small decor, textiles, and crochet items — never hold those on price alone. Where n < 10 the data is thin; lean on general judgment rather than these bands.

## What good listings look like
- "Foldable double bed n bed set up on sale" — NPR 15,000
- "🔥 Urgent Sale: Premium Bed + Wardrobe Combo (LIKE NEW)" — NPR 90,000
- "Hilton gas stove on sale" — NPR 1,000
- "Decorative Ceramic Face Vases" — NPR 1,150
- "Display rack for sale" — NPR 12,000

A good listing names the specific item type plus a brand, material, or condition detail, at a price inside its subcategory band. Emoji-heavy bilingual (English/Nepali) reseller-style titles are common and routinely approved here — do not hold on formatting alone.

## Category-specific hold signals
- The only editor rejection in this category was "fake": hold when photos look like stock/catalog images and the listing reads as a fictitious product rather than a real household item for sale (especially high-value furniture with no specifics).
- A premium furniture set or major household item listed at a token price (e.g., a bed + wardrobe combo for a few hundred NPR) is placeholder or bait pricing → hold and ask for the real price.
- Titles too vague to identify any item at a non-trivial price (e.g., a bare single word like "torso" or a name alone at NPR 5,000) → hold for clarification; buyers cannot tell what is being sold.
